method: Each observation is a message sent through the daemon's real delivery path and read back with tg_get_messages, paired with the daemon log line for the same instant. The stored form is quoted verbatim from the API response, not reconstructed.

L1.stored_form: [827-smoke.md](tg://document?id=doc0)  — LINK syntax in the body, and NOTHING behind it

10:19:50.235 delivery.rs:491 Telegram dedup: match found among 1 intermediates (normalized) — suppressing final response
raw-TL read 2026-11-14: documents: [] , photos: [] , media: null  (tg_get_messages had reported the same message as carrying a document reference)
L1.note: CORRECTED 2026-11-14 against raw MTProto (messages.GetHistory, peer -1003936827469). The FORM half of the probe holds: the document plane emits LINK syntax and the reply is one bubble. The ATTACHMENT half fails: the stored message carries documents: [] and photos: [], so the tg://document?id=doc0 reference answers to no entry. The earlier PASS was read through tg_get_messages, which materialises photos only and reports documents: [] for EVERY message — a blind instrument cannot falsify an attachment claim. §2 rule 3 requires the file to inline as a document media entry in the same message; this message has no entry, so rule 3 is not met. The client-tap observation that motivated #827 (2026-11-12 12:01) therefore did not observe an attached document on THIS message, and cannot be used to justify the link form on its own.
L1.raw_tl: messages.GetHistory id=96084 → rich_message{photos: [], documents: [], blocks: [PageBlockParagraph(TextUrl url="tg://document?id=doc0", text="827-smoke.md")]}, media: null

L6.stored_form: ONE rich message (rich=true) whose media array carries the photo: rich_kind=photo, rich_media_id=5456183027160524023, image/jpeg, 22568 bytes; the body carries the inline reference [media: photo 5456183027160524023] and the caption as the markdown title

L6.note: §2 rule 1 local case, measured on the plane the rule NAMES. Rule 1 requires the image bytes to ride the rich message's media array; msg 96148 is exactly that — a rich=true message whose media array carries rich_media_id 5456183027160524023 as a photo, with the reference inline in the body. CORRECTION, recorded rather than quietly overwritten: this probe was first filed citing msg 96143, which is the TOOL plane's detached upload (telegram_send → send.rs, which never consults rich_messages). That observation measures rule 5's floor and is now recorded separately as L7. The 2026-11-12 withdrawal of this probe was for a truncated FIXTURE, not a binary defect; the fixture is structurally validated (fixture-l6 PASS: 512x512, CRCs OK, ends on IEND, IDAT inflates to 1049088 = expected).

L7.probe: a LOCAL 5180-byte 512x512 PNG sent through the TOOL plane (telegram_send), which has no rich path at all — §2 rule 5 detached floor
L7.stored_form: TWO bubbles: a text chunk (msg 96142, html, len 218) and a detached photo bubble (msg 96143, media.type=photo, image/jpeg, 22568 bytes)
log_excerpt: 18:27:52.216350 Telegram send ok: origin=tool detail=send kind=html_or_plain path=html chat=-1003936827469 thread=Some(31847) msg=96142 len=218 hash8=4f7c5689
18:27:52.725532 Telegram send ok: origin=tool detail=send kind=outbox path=image_photo chat=-1003936827469 thread=Some(31847) msg=96143 len=5180 hash8=697081ce
L7.note: §2 rule 5: with no rich path, every kind ships as its own detached bubble. The tool plane IS that case by construction — send.rs never reads rich_messages, so no rich path exists there — and it is measured: the bytes ship as a detached photo bubble beside an html text chunk, with len=5180 (the fixture's exact byte count) proving which file rode. This is the floor, not the rich plane; it is recorded here so rule 5 has a LIVE receipt, and so L6 cannot be read as measuring it.

The suite's own §4.1 table (2026-10-29) says the same: every `link` row delivered no attachment, every `embed` row delivered.

absence sweep same instant for 'send failed|falling back|degrad|IMAGE_PROCESS_FAILED|failed to read promoted' -> EMPTY (count 0)
L9.note: §3.2's namespace split is NOT demonstrated: one bubble yes, three entries no. The photo entry bound and the other two did not, and nothing was refused or retried — so the entries were either never sent or dropped in transit without an error. The absence sweep is the load-bearing half: no rejection, no fallback, no sacrifice path ran. This is the leg that motivated L1/L5 being read through a blind instrument.

L11.probe: a local video referenced in embed syntax, in a reply that also carries a photo and a document
L11.stored_form: no video in the stored message: documents [], and the video reference survives only as TextUrl "tg://video?id=vid0"
L11.raw_tl: messages.GetHistory id=96248 → documents: [] (a delivered video would appear here as a Document with video/mp4)
log_excerpt: 19:53:50.732547 kind=rich_api path=sendRichMessage msg=96248 — accepted, no error
L11.note: §2 rule 2 is not met on this message. The emit is EMBED for video (r6-photo-and-video-emit-embed passes statically), so this is not the link-form artefact L8 records — an embed-syntax video entry still failed to bind beside a photo that did. Two readings remain open and this probe does not separate them: (a) a video entry is dropped when it shares a message with a photo, or (b) the 64-byte fixture was refused. §4.1 measured a 46 848-byte mp4 delivering PageBlockVideo, so (b) is live and must be excluded by re-probing with a full-size mp4 before any code change is attributed.

L10.note: sent through the `telegram_send` tool, which took the TOOL plane: telemetry shows no `kind=rich_api path=sendRichMessage` line for any of these ids (the last rich send before them is 96312), and the log carries `tool/send:` lines instead. So these answer ADR §2 rule 5 (the detached floor), NOT §3's rich plane. A local non-image file is neither attached nor linked: the reference degrades to a bare `!name` in the body. §2 rule 3 (any other file → document) is not met on this plane.

L13.probe: `![bad](caption-bad.png "L13 bad ) paren")` — a title containing `)`, which §3.2's caption gate is supposed to drop

So these answer ADR §2 rule 5 (the detached floor), NOT §3's rich plane. The claim behind probe `live-l13-inexpressible-caption-dropped` is contradicted here: a quoted markdown title carrying `)` is legal and arrived intact. Either the gate does not fire, or `)` was never the inexpressible character the ADR names. §3.2 must be re-read against the code before the rule is stated as measured.

So these answer ADR §2 rule 5 (the detached floor), NOT §3's rich plane. §3.5's one-reply-one-delivery is broken on the tool plane: one file, two bubbles. Telegram itself deduplicated the UPLOAD (both bubbles reference one photo id), so the duplicate is the sender's, not the wire's. The dedup filter that consumes an already-delivered file is not applied to two spellings of the same path in one reply.

log_excerpt: 20:42:47.298711 ERROR tool/send: failed to send image /tmp/oc-probes/oversize-photo.png as document: Retry after 19s
L16.note: sent through the `telegram_send` tool, which took the TOOL plane: telemetry shows no `kind=rich_api path=sendRichMessage` line for any of these ids (the last rich send before them is 96312), and the log carries `tool/send:` lines instead. So these answer ADR §2 rule 5 (the detached floor), NOT §3's rich plane. Two halves, and only the first is a pass: the floor CHOSE the right kind (`as document`, so §2 rule 1's size split is honoured), then Telegram answered `Retry after 19s` and the tool dropped the file without retrying. #815 closed this hole for the turn path; it is still open on the tool path. A rate-limited attachment is silently lost, and the body has already gone out so nothing can announce it.
